(f) "notification" means a notification published in the Official Gazette;
(g) "owner", when used in relation to a textile undertaking, means any person or firm who or which is, immediately before the appointed day, the immediate proprietor or lessee or occupier of the textile undertaking or any part thereof, and in the case of a textile company which is being wound up or the business whereof is being carried on by a liquidator or receiver, includes such liquidator or receiver, and also includes any agent or manager of such owner but does not include any person or body of persons authorised under the Textile Undertakings (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1983 (40 of 1983) or under the Laxmirattan and Atherton West Cotton Mills (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1976 (98 of 1976) to take over the management of the whole or any part of the textile undertaking;

(l) "textile company" means a company (being a company as defined in the Companies Act, 1956) (1 of 1956) specified in column (3) of the First Schedule as owning the textile undertaking specified in the corresponding entry in column (2) of that Schedule;
(m) "textile undertaking" or 'the textile undertaking" means an undertaking specified in column (2) of the First Schedule, the management of which was before the appointed day, taken over by the Central Government under the Textile Undertakings (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1983 (40 of 1983), or as the case may be, under the Laxmirattan and Atherton West Cotton Mills (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1976 (98 of 1976).

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Right to Information Act, 2005 (RTI Act, 2005)
Key Provisions
1.	Right to Information
•	All citizens have the right to information, subject to the Act's provisions.
2.	Obligations of Public Authorities
•	Maintain, computerize, and network records for easy access.
•	Publish various details about the authority.
•	Provide reasons for administrative or quasi-judicial decisions.
•	Suo motu disclosure of information.
3.	Designation of Public Information Officers
•	Designate Central/State Public Information Officers and Assistants.
4.	Exemptions and Penalties
•	Exemptions: For certain organisations with exceptions.
•	Penalties: Include fines and imprisonment for non-compliance or misconduct.
5.	Information Commissions
•	Establishment of Central and State Information Commissions.
6.	Miscellaneous
•	Protection of Action in Good Faith
•	Overriding Effect
•	Bar on Court Jurisdiction
•	Monitoring and Reporting

dc.identifier.preamble_description.value:
THE RIGHT TO INFORMATION ACT, 2005
ACT NO. 22 OF 2005

[15th June, 2005.]

An Act to provide for setting out the practical regime of right to information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, the constitution of a Central Information Commission and State Information Commissions and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
WHEREAS the Constitution of India has established democratic Republic;
AND WHEREAS democracy requires an informed citizenry and transparency of information which are vital to its functioning and also to contain corruption and to hold Governments are their instrumentalities accountable to the governed;
AND WHEREAS revelation of information in actual practice is likely to conflict with other public interests including efficient operations of the Governments, optimum use of limited fiscal resources and the preservation of confidentiality of sensitive information;
AND WHEREAS it is necessary to harmonise these conflicting interests while preserving the paramountcy of the democratic ideal;
Now, THEREFORE, it is expendient to provide for furnishing certain information to citizens who desire to have it.
BE it enacted by Parliament in the Fifty-sixth Year of the Republic of India as follows:--

dc.legislation.history.value:
Legislative History:

The Right to Information Act, 2005

Short Title - The Right to Information Act, 2005

Act Number / Year - Act No. 22 of 2005

Act ID (India Code) - 200522 (Internal ID: 2005-22)

Introduced In - Lok Sabha (as The Right to Information Bill, 2004)

Presidential Assent Date - June 15, 2005

Official Gazette Publication - June 21, 2005

Enforcement Strategy - Phase 1 (Immediate provisions): June 15, 2005 (Ss. 4(1), 5(1)-(2), 12, 13, 15, 16, 24, 27, 28); Phase 2 (Full Enforcement): October 12, 2005 (120th day of enactment)

Nodal Ministry - Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions

Precedent & Statutory Rationale

1. Replacement of the Weak 2002 Framework:

o The preceding Freedom of Information Act, 2002 was widely criticized for containing excessive exemptions, weak enforcement mechanisms, and lacking proactive disclosure mandates. It was never notified into force.

2. Promotion of Transparency and Accountability:

o Enacted to provide a practical regime for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, thereby combating systemic corruption, promoting governmental transparency, and establishing independent appeal bodies.

Parliamentary Trajectory & Enactment

• December 2004: The Right to Information Bill, 2004 was introduced in the Lok Sabha, reflecting wide inputs from the National Advisory Council (NAC) and civil society organizations.

• May 2005: Passed by the Lok Sabha (May 11, 2005) and Rajya Sabha (May 12, 2005) with significant amendments strengthening penalty structures and disclosure rules.

• June 15, 2005: Received Presidential Assent as Act No. 22 of 2005.

• October 12, 2005: Came into full operational effect across India upon the completion of the 120-day statutory transition window.

Core Statutory Framework Established

1. Obligation of Public Authorities (Section 4): Mandates every public authority to maintain records duly cataloged and proactively publish vast categories of administrative data.

2. Public Information Officers (Section 5): Requires public authorities to designate Central/State Public Information Officers (CPIOs/SPIOs) to process information requests within strict timeframes (typically 30 days).

3. Information Commissions (Sections 12 & 15): Establishes the autonomous Central Information Commission (CIC) and State Information Commissions (SICs) vested with powers of a civil court to penalize non-compliance and hear second appeals

Source: Official Records of Parliament, India Code, and Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions

dc.identifier.next_section.value: 50.Restrictions on Chairperson or Judicial Member or Technical or Administrative Member on employment after cessation of office.

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
(1) The appropriate Government may, in consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court, remove from office of the Chairperson or any Judicial Member or Technical or Administrative Member of the Appellate Tribunal, who—
(a) has been adjudged as an insolvent; or
(b) has been convicted of an offence which, in the opinion of the appropriate Government involves moral turpitude; or
(c) has become physically or mentally incapable; or
(d) has acquired such financial or other interest as is likely to affect prejudicially his functions; or
(e) has so abused his position as to render his continuance in office prejudicial to the public interest.
(2) The Chairperson or Judicial Member or Technical or Administrative Member shall not be removed from his office except by an order made by the appropriate Government after an inquiry made by the Judge of the High Court in which such Chairperson or Judicial Member or Technical or Administrative Member has been informed of the charges against him and given a reasonable opportunity of being heard in respect of those charges.
(3) The appropriate Government may suspend from the office of the Chairperson or Judicial Member or Technical or Administrative Member in respect of whom a reference of conducting an inquiry has been made to the Judge of the High Court under sub-section (2), until the appropriate Government passes an order on receipt of the report of inquiry made by the Judge of the High Court on such reference.
(4) The appropriate Government may, by rules, regulate the procedure for inquiry referred to in sub-section (2).
